objectives: Use diagnostic evidence to identify the weakest /l/ component.
Deliver targeted remediation for recognition, decoding, encoding, comprehension, or fluency.
Use fresh items to reassess the repaired skill.
Route learners forward only when mastery criteria are met.
concepts: Remediation should target the specific error pattern.
Fresh assessment items provide evidence of transferable learning.
Mastery requires adequate performance across critical components.
A learner can need remediation in one component while retaining strength in others.

definitions.definition: Instruction and practice focused on a specific identified learning gap.
A fresh measurement used to determine whether the targeted skill has improved.
A new assessment item that measures the same skill without repeating the exact prior question.

workedExamples: Weak sound recognition → auditory /l/ versus /r/ discrimination → fresh recognition check.
Weak encoding → segment CVC words → map phonemes to graphemes → fresh spelling check.
Weak comprehension → controlled sentence questions → fresh text-evidence check.
commonMistakes: Remediating every skill when only one component is weak.
Advancing because of speed despite inaccurate decoding.

conceptual: Match an error pattern to the correct remediation activity.
application: Select a targeted response based on diagnostic evidence.
higherOrderThinking: Interpret mixed component results and choose the narrowest effective remediation route.
mixedReview: Reassess /l/ skills across recognition, decoding, encoding, comprehension, and fluency.

quickRevision: diagnose → target → practise → fresh reassess → route
formulaOrFactBank: Advance = reassessment ≥ 0.80 + no critical weak component.
mistakeBasedRevision: Match each error to its component before choosing remediation.
weakTopicRevision: Repeat only the weak component with varied fresh examples until mastery evidence is sufficient.

activities.name: Route decision
steps: Advance if all criteria are met.
Otherwise assign the next targeted remediation.

outcomes: Learner receives remediation matched to the identified /l/ weakness.
Learner demonstrates improvement on fresh reassessment items.
System can route the learner to advancement or further targeted remediation.

routing.advance: Advance when reassessment is at least 0.80 and no critical component remains below target.
routing.remediate: Reteach only the component that remains below target, then issue another fresh reassessment.

questions.question: If a learner confuses /l/ and /r/, which practice is most direct?
options: Listen, identify /l/ versus /r/, then repeat the target sound.

questions.question: Which word begins with /l/ and ends with /p/?
A learner writes “lap” for “lip.” Which component needs reteaching?
A learner reads “log” as “lag.” What should they check?
A learner can decode “lip” but reads it slowly. What is the best practice?
options: Repeated accurate reading of controlled /l/ words and sentences.
Guess the word from a picture.

questions.question: Which activity targets comprehension rather than decoding?
options: Answering who/what/where questions from a controlled sentence.

questions.question: A learner scores below target only in spelling. What is the most targeted route?
options: Phoneme segmentation, sound-to-letter mapping, and fresh spelling items.

questions.question: Why should reassessment use fresh items?
options: To check whether the learner can apply the skill beyond memorised answers.

questions.question: Which result supports advancement after reassessment?
options: At least 80% with no critical weak component.
Correct answers only on memorised items.

questions.question: If comprehension remains below target after decoding improves, what should happen?
options: Provide targeted comprehension practice and reassess comprehension.
Restart all phonics from the beginning.

questions.question: What is the purpose of targeted remediation?
options: Repair the specific weak skill and verify improvement with reassessment.
Give identical practice to every learner.
